findings.title: Table widget flag renders an empty table
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` flag is on, `tableResultComponent` ignores the loaded widget result and always mounts `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and `tableData` set to empty `data`/`fields`/`units`. Every dashboard table widget behind that flag shows no columns and no rows, while the previous `StyledSimpleTableChart` path (which had `result.data`, fields, and metadata) is skipped. The flag cannot be turned on without blanking table widgets.

findings.title: Error payloads are zipped against dict values, not ids
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds node ids from `error_ids`, then pairs `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id; missing keys are omitted and value order is not guaranteed to match `error_ids`. The resulting `ErrorEvent.id` can be attached to the wrong event, and a missing event shifts every subsequent id. Look up each node id explicitly (and skip missing keys) instead of zipping parallel lists.

findings.title: Summarize never requests error_ids
findings.body: Error context is taken from `process_raw_response(..., fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` and then `response[0].get("error_ids", [])`. This endpoint does not force `error_ids` into the Snuba field list, so a normal summarize GET (no `field` query param) gets no error ids, `fetch_error_details` is a no-op, and the new error-context logs are never sent to Seer. The field list should always include `error_ids` regardless of the caller.

findings.title: Nodestore timestamps are not numeric
findings.body: Error events copy `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` straight into `ErrorEvent.timestamp`. Nodestore event payloads store `timestamp` as an ISO-8601 string, while replay segment events use unix floats. `get_request_data` sorts on that value and `gen_request_data` compares it with `event.get("timestamp", 0)`. A string-vs-float comparison raises TypeError, which is uncaught in `analyze_recording_segments`, so any replay that actually has stored errors fails the summarize request with 500 instead of merging error lines.

findings.title: Reports with neither age nor timestamp are accepted
findings.body: `age` and `timestamp` are both `required=False`, and the cross-field checks only run when that field is present. A report that omits both (or sends only the other required fields) passes `BrowserReportSerializer` and is counted as a valid browser report. The comments say both Reporting API specs must be supported; each spec requires exactly one of those time fields. `validate()` should reject payloads that have neither or both. `validate_timestamp` also uses `initial_data.get("age")`, so `age: 0` is treated as absent and will not fail the timestamp check.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only filtered while searching
findings.body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is applied only inside the branch that runs when `searchQuery` is non-empty. With an empty search the full sorted attribute list is returned, so those fields still render in the default Attributes tree. When the user searches, the same names are dropped even if they match the query. The exclusion needs to apply before the search filter if those attributes are meant to be hidden.

findings.title: Analytics recorded before feature and auth checks
findings.body: `analytics.record(..., user_id=request.user.id)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before body validation. This endpoint allows org-auth-token callers (`is_org_auth_token_auth` later). If `request.user` is missing or is not a real user, `.id` raises and a disabled or token-authenticated assemble call 500s instead of returning 404/400. It also emits assemble analytics for requests that are immediately rejected as feature-disabled. Record only after the feature check, and pass `user_id` only when the request has an authenticated user.

findings.title: Issue template truncates via the wrong class
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` but calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`. `_truncate_title` is a staticmethod on `CommitContextIntegration`, not on `PRCommentWorkflow`. Generating a merged-PR comment therefore raises AttributeError unless `PRCommentWorkflow` happens to inherit that method, and GitHub/GitLab workflows call this helper as `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template`. Call `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title` (or `self._truncate_title`) so title truncation does not depend on a class that does not define it.
